title: If M(X) < ∞, then ω ↦ X(χω) is a current on ℝ^P
statement: Let P, q ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set. Let χ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) χ) with tsupport χ ⊆ U and |χ(x)| ≤ 1 for every x. Let X ∈ D_q(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U q) have finite mass, M(X) = X.mass = X.massOn U ≠ ∞. Then there is Y ∈ D_q(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ q: a linear functional on D^q(ℝ^P) that is sequentially continuous at 0 in the sense of TestFormOnConverges) such that Y(ω) = X(η) for all ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^P) and η ∈ D^q(U) with η(x) = χ(x)·ω(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (χ : Eucl P → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) χ → tsupport χ ⊆ U → (∀ x, |χ x| ≤ 1) → ∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn U q, X.mass ≠ ∞ → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) q, ∀ (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) q) (η : TestFormOn U q), (∀ x, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x = χ x • (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x) → Y ω = X η
